findings.evidence: Description: "RL cells (human diffuse large B-cell lymphoma cell line)"; SDRF characteristics[disease]: "Burkitt lymphoma" in every row.
findings.explanation: The disease annotation contradicts the description, which says the RL line is a diffuse large B-cell lymphoma line. The error is the same in all rows, so it is a run-wide annotation mistake that would give the samples the wrong disease context in a public repository.
findings.suggested_fix: Change characteristics[disease] to "diffuse large B-cell lymphoma" in all rows, after checking the Cellosaurus entry for CVCL_1660.

findings.evidence: Rule check: "4 channel(s) not assigned to a sample: TMT132C, TMT133N, TMT133C, TMT134N." Description: "Four channels are unused."
findings.explanation: Only 12 of the 16 TMTpro channels (TMT126 to TMT132N) are assigned. This matches the description, which says a 16-plex kit was used for 12 samples. The unused channels are expected to be empty and should not affect quantification, though any signal in them would indicate reporter-ion interference or contamination. The likely cause is that the experiment has 12 samples and the kit has 16 channels.
findings.suggested_fix: No change needed to the SDRF if the channels were left empty. Optionally note in the study documentation that TMT132C, TMT133N, TMT133C and TMT134N were unused.

summary: One metadata mismatch: the disease is annotated as Burkitt lymphoma but the description says diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The unused-channel warning is expected, because 12 samples were run in a 16-plex kit, so it is explained rather than treated as a design problem. The other values checked agree with the description: organism, cell line, treatments, antibodies, trypsin, TMTpro and 12 samples.
